Package com.hkust.marketplace.ui

Class Dialogs

java.lang.Object
com.hkust.marketplace.ui.Dialogs
public final class Dialogs extends Object
The dialogs every portal uses, so confirmations, messages and errors look and behave the same everywhere (non-functional requirement: consistent interaction across the three portals). Destructive actions must ask confirm(java.lang.String, java.lang.String) first. 

 if (Dialogs.confirm("Delete listing", "Delete 'Desk Lamp'? This cannot be undone.")) {
     try {
         service.deleteListing(id);
         Dialogs.info("Listing deleted", "'Desk Lamp' was removed.");
     } catch (ServiceException e) {
         Dialogs.problem(e);
     }
 }
This class only shows JavaFX dialogs; checks on what users type are in TextInputs, where they are unit-tested.

    • form

      public static javafx.scene.control.Dialog<javafx.scene.control.ButtonType> form(String title, String header, javafx.scene.control.ButtonType submit, javafx.scene.control.ButtonType cancel)
      An empty form dialog with a heading and two buttons, centred on the app's window, for a screen to fill with its fields: 
      
 Dialog<ButtonType> dialog = Dialogs.form("Make Offer", "Your price offer for 'Desk Lamp'", SUBMIT, ButtonType.CANCEL);
 dialog.getDialogPane().setContent(new VBox(8, new Label("Your price (HK$)"), priceBox));
      A form dialog uses the app's stylesheet, because it has the app's window as its owner.
      Parameters:
      submit - the button that sends the form
      cancel - the button that closes it without sending
